analysis:
I found no concrete regression, but the main behavior change in SandboxSetupCommand.swift was not visible. That unit (4ef4ced1e3c7d2e1:0) has only metadata and a truncated patch excerpt, and the cli-reference.md hunks for setup are also truncated. The visible changes are sandboxes.md docs (added re-plan paragraph at head lines 85-94, troubleshooting at 101-107 and 120-125) and SandboxEligibility.swift.

SandboxEligibility.swift (head 223-227, 268-278, 308-309) is display-only arithmetic. diskShortfall now subtracts the plan's planned slots (plannedBytes) and uses nextSlotBytes. freeSpaceNote prints static text plus a GiB figure. Both are computed from local numbers, with no external input, no shell execution and no secrets. The Int64 arithmetic involves only the plan's slot counts and byte sizes. The plan comes from the installer, which is a TB-013 input. Worst case is a misleading message, not a security impact.

The security-relevant change is described in the setup command's help text (Swift patch excerpt) and sandboxes.md lines 85-94. On an already set-up Mac, `setup` now downloads and runs the sandbox installer again to ask for its plan. It can then reinstall the add-on and restart it, automatically with --yes or with no terminal when the plan only adds slots. This widens how often the TB-013/T-061 trust path is exercised: the installer is downloaded and run as the Mac owner (A-019). Unattended application without an explicit --yes when stdin is not a TTY is an implicit-consent question. Whether the installer's release verification and TLS checks are unchanged is not visible. The docs state the installer refuses while a job runs and that setup never passes --force. That is a claim about the installer, not evidence.

The next pass should check the full SandboxSetupCommand.swift. Items to check: whether the installer is fetched and verified the same way as before, how the non-interactive auto-apply is gated, and whether the guard against replacing the add-on while jobs run (the hold interplay in TB-012/A-018) is enforced. The threat model's TB-013/T-061 may need an update to mention the recurring re-plan download.
